newsitem.title: TURKEY: Solvay - Turk Sisecam signed JV accord.
newsitem.headline: Solvay - Turk Sisecam signed JV accord.

text.p: Turkey's leading glass and chemicals producer Sisecam Group and the Belgian Solvay Group signed a joint venture agreement on Bulgaria's soda ash producer Solvay Sodi, a statement from Sisecam said.
The Turkish group has bought 19 percent of an Austria based joint holding company, Solvay Sisecam Holding AG through which Solvay Group controls Solvay Sodi shares, the statement said.
Solvay Group acquired 60 percent of the former Sodi Devnya of Varna in Bulgaria after the company was privatised in April this year.
The rest of the company is owned by Sodi employees and domestic Bulgarian investors.
The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development also acquired 24 percent of the Austrian holding company in June.
With the joint venture, Sisecam attained the right to purchase a minimum of 25 percent of Sodi's total output each year for marketing it freely and independently.
Solvay Sodi is the largest running synthetic soda ash production facility in the world with an annual output capacity of 1.2 million tonnes.

The newly elected board of directors decided to invest up to $25 million to double its dense soda ash capacity from 400,000 tonnes to 800,000 tonnes and to build a new 18,000 tonnes silo to improve the company's storage facilities.
The investment, to be completed by the last quarter of 1998, will be the first step of a five-years investment program of $67 million, to increase further the production capacity of dense soda ash.

Solvay group is the world leader in soda ash, with $8.8 billion total sales in 1996, generated in chemicals, plastics, processing and pharmaceuticals. Solvay, based in Brussels, employs more than 35,000 people in 41 countries.
Turkey's Sisecam group is the leading glass and chemicals producer with 1.2 million tonnes of glass and 750,000 tonnes of soda ash annual production capacities.
Sisecam Group generated a total turnover of $1.2 billion in 1996 and employs about 14,500 people.
